question: When did the ozone levels in the atmosphere start to reduce?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1980.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ozone layer**

 
 
• A portion of **Earth's stratosphere** known as the ozone layer or **ozone shield** is responsible for **absorbing the majority of the Sun's ultraviolet light.**
 
• In comparison to other regions of the atmosphere, it has a** high concentration of ozone (O3)**, despite being relatively insignificant in comparison to other gases in the stratosphere.
 
• The **average ozone** concentration in the Earth's atmosphere is approximately** 0.3 parts per million**, while the ozone concentration in the** ozone layer is less than 10 parts per million.**
 
• Although its thickness varies seasonally and geographically, the ozone layer is mostly found in the** lower stratosphere**, **between 15 and 35 kilometers (9 to 22 miles)** above the surface of the Earth.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Depletion of ozone layer**

 
 
• Free radical catalysts like** nitric oxide (NO), nitrous oxide (N2O), hydroxyl (OH), atomic chlorine (Cl), **and** atomic bromine (Br)** have the potential to deplete the ozone layer.
 
• Nitrous oxide was the most significant **ozone-depleting substance (ODS)** emitted by humans in** 2009.**
 
• Since the late **1970s**, ozone** levels have decreased **by an average of about **4%** globally.
 
• Around the **north and south poles, **about **5%** of the Earth's surface has experienced much larger seasonal declines that are referred to as **"ozone holes."**
 
• **Joe Farman, Brian Gardiner**, and **Jonathan Shanklin** first made the discovery of the **annual depletion of ozone** above the Antarctic in a paper that was published in Nature on **May 16, 1985.**
